subject: Hosting risk & evidence roadmap — next steps for PulseHealth (HIPAA/BAA asks)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@pulsehealth.com>, Elena Morales <elena.morales@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Hosting risk & evidence roadmap — next steps for PulseHealth (HIPAA/BAA asks)

Hi Sanjay / Elena — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can converge on hosting mode and evidence handoff.

Call recap (TL;DR)
- PulseHealth is HIPAA-regulated; primary asks were BAA + SOC2 evidence and clarity on KMS/data residency for PHI.
- You prefer a predictable performance SLA and operational separation from shared tenants.
- Team is open to Dedicated capacity or Private VPC; on-prem is possible but not preferred due to ops lift.

Redwood suggested hosting options (high level)
1) Hosted API (shared multitenant) — fastest onboarding, lower cost; meets SOC2 controls but requires BAA for PHI; best for low-risk PII/PHI patterns.
2) Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) — single-tenant compute, stronger isolation, supports strict ingress/egress controls, recommended when predictable latency and throughput matter.
3) Private VPC / on-prem — customer-managed network, strongest perimeter control and KMS integration; longer lead time and ops overhead.

Evidence & audit items we can provide now
- SOC2 Type II report (Redwood): attached (SOC2_report_redwood_2025Q4.pdf).
- Standard BAA template: attached (BAA_template_redwood_v1.docx).
- One-pager comparing hosting modes and data flow (deployment_options_onepager.pdf).

Open / action items (proposed ownership)
- PulseHealth: confirm preferred hosting mode (Hosted | Dedicated | Private VPC) and any hard constraints (data residency, key management). (Action: Sanjay)
- Redwood: provide answers on encryption-at-rest, KMS options, retention windows, and provisioning timeline for Dedicated. (Action: Karthik)
- Schedule a technical deep-dive (network & KMS + SIEM/logs) with PulseHealth security and our infra team — propose Wed 20 May, 10:00 PT. (Action: Marissa/All)

If you confirm Dedicated as the preferred path, we’ll kick off a short procurement packet (SOW + BAA) and estimate a 2–4 week provisioning window once contracts are signed (exact timing depends on capacity and region).

Thanks — I’ll coordinate follow-ups once I have your hosting preference.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: SOC2_report_redwood_2025Q4.pdf (pdf), BAA_template_redwood_v1.docx (docx), deployment_options_onepager.pdf (pdf)

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@pulsehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena.morales@pulsehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 18:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosting risk & evidence roadmap — next steps for PulseHealth (HIPAA/BAA asks)

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying q's from our InfoSec/Cloud team:

1) Encryption & KMS
- Do you support customer-managed keys (CMKs) for encryption at rest? If so, which KMS providers can we integrate (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault)?
2) Data residency / logging
- Can you guarantee logs and audit trails for PHI access are stored in our chosen region and retained for at least 7 years?
3) SOC2 scope
- Which services are included in your SOC2 report (hosting, runtime, console/ops)? We need to map controls to our vendor risk framework.

Operational preference
- We want to avoid on-prem if possible due to limited ops headcount. Leaning toward Dedicated capacity if the BAA & KMS options check out.

I’m attaching PulseHealth_Security_Questionnaire_2026.docx — it’s long but will help you map exactly which artifacts we need for procurement/legal. Please have your infra/security team review and we’ll aim to confirm hosting preference by EOD Tuesday.

— Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Cloud Security | PulseHealth
sanjay@pulsehealth.com

Attachment: PulseHealth_Security_Questionnaire_2026.docx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@pulsehealth.com>, Elena Morales <elena.morales@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosting risk & evidence roadmap — next steps for PulseHealth (HIPAA/BAA asks)

Thanks Sanjay — quick answers below to the questions you raised. I’ve pasted the key bits for the questionnaire we usually see.

> 1) Do you support customer-managed keys (CMKs)?
Yes. For Dedicated and Private VPC deployments we support CMKs via AWS KMS (and we can accept imported key material where required). For Hosted API we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys by default; customers can opt into CMK-backed envelopes in select regions. For on-prem, you bring your HSM and we can integrate via our connector. See attached KMS_flow_diagram.png for a high-level flow.

> 2) Data residency & logging retention
- Logs: audit logs (who/what/when) are stored in the tenant-specific logging bucket in the customer region for Dedicated and Private VPC. Hosted API log retention is configurable; by default 90 days but we can extend per contract.
- Retention windows: we can support 7+ years retention for audit logs for Dedicated/Private (SLA & cost will be in procurement).

> 3) SOC2 scope
Our SOC2 Type II (attached) covers our control environment for the inference runtime, orchestration layer, and the Redwood Console (control plane). It explicitly calls out change management, access controls, encryption, and monitoring. For Dedicated we provide additional host-level attestation and can supply tailored evidence during your assessment.

Provisioning & timelines
- Dedicated: typical bench-to-prod provisioning is ~3 weeks after PO & contract (includes capacity reservation, networking, and customer key onboarding).
- BAA: our template is attached; legal usually turns around redlines within 3–5 business days for standard terms.

Proposed next steps
1) Confirm hosting preference (Dedicated preferred per your note).
2) Share the names of your procurement & legal contacts (we’ll add them to the SOW/BAA exchange).
3) Lock in the technical deep-dive: Wed 20 May 10:00 PT — we’ll cover KMS integration, VPC peering, and logging/alerts.

If helpful I can also pull a short reference list of current healthcare customers on Dedicated — ping me and I’ll share names and contact windows.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Infrastructure Product | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.inference

Attachment: KMS_flow_diagram.png

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@pulsehealth.com>

Karthik / Marissa — thanks for the quick answers and materials. We reviewed with procurement and security during the call:

Decision & immediate asks
- PulseHealth will proceed with Dedicated capacity. Key conditions: CMK support for keys (AWS KMS preferred), audit log retention to 7 years, and execution of BAA prior to any PHI onboarding.
- Please add our procurement contact Priya Singh (priya.singh@pulsehealth.com) to the SOW/BAA thread — she’ll own PO timelines.

Next steps from Redwood
- Share a short addendum that spells out CMK onboarding steps and timeline.
- Confirm Dedicated provisioning ETA and any prerequisites for VPC peering.
- Legal: start the BAA exchange (we’ll have Priya & our counsel looped).

We’ll plan to run the tech deep-dive now on the calendar as discussed. Looking forward to the KMS flow diagram and SOC2 document.

— Sanjay
Head of Cloud Security | PulseHealth

Forwarded message: please include Priya on the procurement thread and send the PO template when available.
